description: The parties of the UBL example world: their place on the map, what they do and their identity.

parties.name: Raw Material Supplier
parties.what: Mines the ore at the start of the chain and sells it to the manufacturer.
parties.how: A mine sells a few products in large volumes to a small number of customers. With UBL, its orders, despatch advices and invoices carry the same quantities, lot numbers and weights from the first document to the last, so the buyer can match them without retyping weighbridge tickets.

site.description: The mine and its rail siding
site.conditions: Unpaved access road; heavy vehicles only.

parties.name: Manufacturer
parties.what: Makes park benches and street furniture: frames from steel made from the mine's ore, slats from the sawmill in Bayvarra, packed in recycled packaging from Bayvarra. Sells to the distributor abroad and tenders in public procurement.
parties.how: The manufacturer sits in the middle of the chain: it buys, produces, sells, exports and tenders. UBL gives it one vocabulary for all of that, from the order it places with the mine to the certificate of origin and the tender it submits to a public buyer, so the same item, party and price data are reused instead of re-entered for every partner.

parties.name: Seller's Warehouse (3PL)
parties.what: Picks, packs and hands the goods to the carrier for the manufacturer; knows nothing about prices.
parties.how: A third-party warehouse acts on instructions from its client but never sees the commercial terms. UBL separates the two: the warehouse sends despatch advices and inventory reports with exactly the logistic details (packages, weights, serial numbers) while prices stay in the documents between seller and buyer.

parties.name: Waste Processor
parties.what: Takes production waste from the manufacturer and invoices the removal.
parties.how: Waste movements must be announced and tracked before the waste leaves the site. UBL's waste notification and waste movement documents describe the waste, its producer and the facility that recovers or disposes of it, and the same parties then appear on the invoice for the removal service.

parties.name: Rail Carrier
parties.what: Runs the ore trains from the mine to the factory and container trains to the border.
parties.how: A rail carrier plans capacity on a fixed timetable. UBL transport documents let its customers request and confirm transport plans and receive status updates per train and wagon, with the same consignment references the forwarder and the receiving terminal use.

parties.name: Road Carrier
parties.what: Trucks the goods across the land border to the distributor; last-mile delivery.
parties.how: Road carriers handle many short jobs with frequent changes. With UBL they receive transport instructions, report status at each stop and invoice the freight in one structured format, so every customer, large or small, can process them automatically.

parties.name: Inland Waterway Carrier
parties.what: Moves bulk on the river from Urvania down to the coast of Bayvarra.
parties.how: Inland waterway transport moves large volumes slowly. UBL transport execution plans and waybills carry the barge, the loading and discharge quays and the cargo per hold, so shippers and terminals can plan around long transit times.

parties.name: Rail Hub / Intermodal Terminal
parties.what: Transfers containers between rail and road at the border; manages tracks and slots.
parties.how: An intermodal terminal is where rail and road meet. UBL status messages and transport reports let it tell carriers and forwarders when a container arrived, was transferred or left, using the same equipment and consignment identifiers on both sides of the transfer.

parties.name: Seller's Bank
parties.what: Holds the manufacturer's account and receives the payments from abroad.
parties.how: The seller's bank receives payments from many countries. Because UBL invoices carry the payee account and a payment reference, and remittance advices repeat that reference, incoming payments can be matched to the right invoices automatically.

parties.name: Chamber of Commerce (XU)
parties.what: Certifies the origin of the exported goods and issues ATA carnets.
parties.how: A chamber of commerce certifies that goods come from where the exporter says. UBL certificate-of-origin and goods-item-passport documents carry the application, the endorsements and the goods in a form customs on the other side can read and verify.

parties.name: Customs (XU)
parties.what: Export customs at the land border crossing.
parties.how: Export customs needs to know what leaves the country, for whom and how. UBL customs declarations reuse the parties, goods and transport details already present in the commercial and transport documents, so the declarant does not have to collect them again.

parties.name: Identifier Issuing Agency
parties.what: Issues item and property identifiers used across the world (a fictional numbering organisation).
parties.how: Everyone in the world refers to the same products and properties. An identifier issuing agency gives those items and properties stable identifiers, which UBL documents carry in their identification elements, so a catalogue line, an order line and an invoice line point to exactly the same thing.

parties.name: Customs (XB)
parties.what: Import customs at the land border crossing and at the seaport.
parties.how: Import customs checks goods arriving over the land border and through the seaport. UBL import and transit declarations carry the same consignment and goods data as the export declaration on the other side, which makes it possible to compare them.

identity.name: Customs and Border Service of Bayvarra

parties.name: Distributor
parties.what: Buys finished goods from #5, stocks them in its distribution centre, publishes the catalogue and sells to #26 and overseas to #1.
parties.how: The distributor publishes the catalogue its customers order from, buys from manufacturers and sells at home and overseas. UBL links all of it: catalogue items appear unchanged in orders, orders are referenced by despatch advices and invoices, and receipt advices confirm what actually arrived.

parties.name: Retailer
parties.what: Buys from the distributor, sells to consumers; shares forecasts and promotions.
parties.how: A retailer buys from the distributor and sells to consumers. Besides orders and invoices, UBL lets it share forecasts, promotions and sales data with its supplier, and issue a structured purchase receipt to the consumer.

parties.name: Consumer
parties.what: A private person buying in the shop; receives a purchase receipt.
parties.how: A consumer rarely deals with UBL directly, but a structured purchase receipt means the receipt can be stored, searched or used for a warranty claim without a paper slip.

parties.name: Contracting Authority
parties.what: A public body that buys under procurement law: publishes notices, receives and evaluates tenders.
parties.how: A contracting authority has to buy in a transparent and comparable way. UBL tendering documents take it from the prior information notice to the contract award, so tenders arrive in a structured form that can be checked and evaluated consistently.

identity.name: Lumeport Public Works Department
identity.tax_exemption: Public bodies are exempt from the state sales tax

parties.name: Consortium Partner
parties.what: Tenders together with the manufacturer as consortium partner or subcontractor.
parties.how: A consortium partner tenders together with a main tenderer. UBL tenders and qualification documents name each partner and its qualifications separately, so the authority can see who contributes what.

parties.name: Review Body
parties.what: Independent body that handles appeals and mediation in public procurement.
parties.how: A review body handles appeals against procurement decisions. The tendering documents name it, with the deadlines for an appeal, so every tenderer knows where and when to go.

parties.name: Government Information Service
parties.what: Publishes procurement notices and keeps the business registry.
parties.how: A government information service publishes procurement notices and keeps the business registry. UBL notices reach it in one structured format, and business information documents let it share registry data that tenderers can reuse as evidence.

parties.name: Digital Agreement Governor
parties.what: Governs the multilateral digital agreement under which the parties exchange UBL documents.
parties.how: A digital agreement sets out which documents the participants exchange and under which rules. UBL's digital agreement and digital capability documents describe that framework, and its governor keeps it up to date for all participants.

parties.name: Factor
parties.what: Buys the distributor's receivables and becomes the payee on its invoices.
parties.how: A factor buys the distributor's invoices and collects the payment. UBL invoices can name the factor as payee, with its account, so the buyer pays the right party without a separate letter.

parties.name: Bank / Guarantor
parties.what: Bayvarra's bank: holds the accounts of the distributor, its customers and the public buyer, and issues guarantees, such as the bid bond for a tender.
parties.how: A guarantor stands surety, for example for a bid bond in a tender. UBL's guarantee certificate names the guarantee, the tenderer and the contracting authority, so the authority can check it is valid.

parties.name: Insurer
parties.what: Insures the cargo on its way overseas.
parties.how: An insurer covers the cargo while it travels. UBL transport documents can carry the insurance policy with the insurer, the policy holder and the insured value, so every party in the transport chain knows the goods are covered.

parties.name: Freight Forwarder
parties.what: Books the transport, consolidates shipments and prepares the export documents; also arranges cargo insurance.
parties.how: A freight forwarder organises transport for others. It uses UBL forwarding instructions, packing lists and manifests to combine shipments, book carriers and arrange insurance, keeping one consignment reference across all of them.

parties.name: Seaport (XB)
parties.what: Port of loading: berths, container yard and vessel traffic.
parties.how: The seaport loads the ship. UBL transport reports and status messages tell the port which containers are coming, and tell carriers and authorities what was loaded, on which vessel and when.

parties.name: Ocean Carrier
parties.what: Sails the container ship to the island and issues the negotiable bill of lading.
parties.how: The ocean carrier issues the bill of lading, the document that represents the goods at sea. With UBL that document, the vessel reports and the status updates share the same consignment and container references as the forwarder's booking.

parties.name: Airport (XB)
parties.what: Air cargo terminal for urgent shipments overseas.
parties.how: The airport handles urgent cargo. UBL status messages let it report acceptance, loading and departure, with the air waybill reference the carrier and forwarder use.

parties.name: Seaport (XL)
parties.what: Port of discharge on the island.
parties.how: The island's seaport discharges the ship. It receives the same UBL transport report the loading port sent, so it can plan berths and inform customs before the vessel arrives.

parties.name: Airport (XL)
parties.what: The island's airport, where the air cargo arrives.
parties.how: The island's airport receives the air cargo and reports its arrival to the carrier and the consignee in UBL status messages.

parties.name: Air Carrier
parties.what: The island's airline; flies urgent cargo and uses road feeder services on the mainland.
parties.how: The air carrier flies urgent shipments and uses road feeder services on the mainland. UBL waybills can name the road carrier as substitute carrier, so the whole route, by truck and by plane, stays under one transport document.

parties.name: Customs (XL)
parties.what: Import customs on the island.
parties.how: Import customs on the island receives a declaration that reuses the data of the export side and the transport documents, which speeds up clearance at the port.

parties.name: Customs Declarant / Broker
parties.what: Licensed agent that files the import declaration for the buyer; also acts as tax representative.
parties.how: A customs declarant files declarations for importers and can act as their tax representative. UBL gives it the commercial, transport and customs data in one vocabulary, so it can assemble the declaration from documents it already receives.

parties.name: Buyer's Warehouse (3PL)
parties.what: Receives the goods for the buyer and confirms what arrived.
parties.how: The buyer's warehouse receives the goods. Its UBL receipt advice confirms what arrived, per line and per package, which lets the buyer approve the invoice for exactly what was delivered.

parties.name: Commercial Buyer
parties.what: Needs the goods: orders from the distributor overseas and pays the invoice.
parties.how: The commercial buyer orders overseas and pays across borders. UBL lets it order from the distributor's catalogue, follow the goods through despatch and transport, match the invoice to the order and the receipt, and send a remittance advice with its payment.

parties.name: Buyer's Bank
parties.what: Holds the buyer's account and sends the payment abroad.
parties.how: The buyer's bank sends the payment abroad. The payment reference and payee account come straight from the UBL invoice, so the payment arrives with the information the seller's bank needs to match it.

parties.name: Chamber of Commerce (XL)
parties.what: Guarantees ATA carnets on the import side.
parties.how: The chamber of commerce on the island guarantees goods-item passports for goods that enter temporarily, so customs can accept them without duties.

parties.name: Maritime Administration
parties.what: The island's flag state administration; issues ship security certificates.
parties.how: The island's maritime administration issues ship security certificates. UBL transport reports to the port carry the certificate and its issuer, so the port can check them before the ship arrives.

parties.name: Electricity Utility
parties.what: Generates and supplies electricity in Urvania; its biggest customer is the factory.
parties.how: A utility bills thousands of connections every month. UBL separates the bill (the Invoice) from the consumption behind it (the Utility Statement with meter readings per connection), so a customer with many sites can check each one automatically and a household gets the same structured bill as a factory.

parties.name: Water Utility
parties.what: Supplies drinking water in Coastal State, to shops and households.
parties.how: Water is billed on metered consumption. With UBL the Utility Statement carries the meter readings and the Invoice the amount; the tax exemption for water is stated explicitly, and a Reminder follows the same structure when a household pays late.

parties.name: Telecom Utility
parties.what: The island's telephone and data provider.
parties.how: Telecom bills list calls, data and subscriptions per line. The UBL Utility Statement has a telecommunications structure of its own, so a business customer can allocate the costs of each line without retyping a paper bill.

parties.name: Sawmill
parties.what: Fells timber in the forests of Upland State and saws it into planks, slats and beams; sells slats for the benches across the border and timber to the furniture maker.
parties.how: Wood is sold by dimensions and volume, in lots. UBL carries the measurements and the lot of every item in quotations, orders and despatch advices, so a buyer that orders slats to size gets exactly what it ordered and can trace each lot.

parties.name: Furniture Maker
parties.what: Makes wooden furniture from the sawmill's timber; supplies the department store and furnishes public offices, installation included.
parties.how: A supplier to a retailer shares more than orders: sales per store, stock policies and agreed exception thresholds. UBL's retail collaboration documents carry them, and a Work Report documents installation work for the customer to approve.

parties.name: Textile Mill
parties.what: Spins and weaves the island's cotton into fabric and makes clothing for the department store.
parties.how: Its raw material comes from overseas on a schedule. UBL forecasts and their revisions tell the ginnery what to expect, and the bill of lading, customs documents and invoice of every shipment arrive in one structure.

parties.name: Packaging Maker
parties.what: Makes packaging from recycled plastic granulate that arrives by barge from Urvania; packs the benches and the clothing.
parties.how: Recycled raw material comes in bulk lots by river; packaging goes out in many small orders. UBL handles both with the same order, despatch and invoice structure, across the border and at home.

parties.name: Cotton Farm
parties.what: Grows cotton on the island and delivers the seed cotton to the ginnery after the harvest.
parties.how: A farm does not write invoices: the ginnery weighs and grades the cotton and bills itself on the farm's behalf. UBL's self-billed invoice and credit note are made for exactly this, and the farm receives a structured statement of what it was paid for.

address.Description: Farm track off Plantation Road, past the cotton fields.

parties.name: Cotton Ginnery
parties.what: Gins the farms' seed cotton into bales and exports them to the textile mill on the mainland: the island's export.
parties.how: The ginnery buys from many farms and sells overseas. UBL covers both sides: self-billing towards the farms, and towards the mill an export with weight statement, goods certificate, customs declaration and invoice.
